page.title: Featured Agent Skill Projects | Suede AI
page.lede: Good tools deserve a closer look.
page.intro: Each project here is reviewed against a pinned commit and accepted with a defined scope. Pick one, read the reviewed source, and start with the setup it actually needs.
page.selection: Editorial features are chosen by the Suede AI team for useful workflows and clear setup. Quality scores on skill pages come from the published rubric and are never changed by a feature, a badge or any business relationship.

nominate.headline: Get your project featured
nominate.body: Submit your repository and the exact skills or plugin in scope. Every accepted listing gets a README badge that links to it. Projects selected for a feature also get an intake review pinned to a commit and their own section on this page.
steps: Request a listing with the repository and the skills or plugin you want reviewed.
Add your listing badge to the README so readers can find your listing.
Ask for a feature review. Projects with clear setup, a defined scope and documented data use are the strongest candidates.

page.services_cta_note: Names a campaign in directory/services-cta.json, rendered after the project list, never inside a project card.

projects.name: Appie
projects.headline: From an idea to an article, a chatbot, or a short link.
projects.summary: Bring Appie’s writing, chatbot and link tools into your agent workflow. Pick the skill for the job and follow its individual setup instructions.

skills.title: Write articles
skills.description: Create author profiles and generate articles through Appie’s hosted MCP service.

skills.title: Build a chatbot
skills.description: Supply knowledge sources, track training and chat with a bot through Appie.

skills.title: Shorten and track links
skills.description: Create short links and retrieve their click statistics from your agent.

projects.setup: Requires an Appie project, project API key and hosted MCP connection. The selected workflow sends its content to Appie; service operations may use credits. Each skill page covers its setup and data use.

projects.name: CoalWash
projects.headline: Understand what your agent carries into every session.
projects.summary: Measure memory and governance-file overhead, run maintenance, and inspect the changes. CoalWash pairs a structured-token guard with transaction snapshots and rollback tools.

capabilities.title: Measure the overhead
capabilities.description: Inspect always-loaded memory and governance files before choosing a maintenance pass.

capabilities.title: Review the changes
capabilities.description: Use snapshots and rollback tools to inspect and recover transaction changes.

capabilities.title: Check structured tokens
capabilities.description: Detect drops in tracked tokens such as paths, numbers and commands. Review prose meaning separately.

projects.setup: Requires Claude Code and Node.js. Install the complete plugin so its commands, hooks and engine are available together.
projects.behavior: The plugin registers SessionStart, Stop, PreToolUse and PostToolUse hooks. Default automatic mode can direct Quick maintenance without a new prompt; Full semantic work requires consent and uses your agent’s model. Stop hooks can hold session completion while maintenance is addressed.
projects.guard_scope: The edit guard snapshots supported Edit, Write and MultiEdit changes to memory and governance files and reports tracked-token drops. Shell writes are outside that edit guard. Token checks do not establish semantic preservation; inspect diffs and rollback results.

projects.name: Costory
projects.headline: Understand your cloud bill and choose the next action.
projects.summary: Investigate cost changes, explore BigQuery spend, and map shared costs to teams with an agent connected to Costory. Four workflows cover discovery, evidence, allocation and review.

skills.title: Investigate BigQuery costs
skills.description: Compare compute and storage billing, explore query and dataset costs, and review allocation options.

skills.title: Explain what changed
skills.description: Trace contributors and timing, check usage and operational evidence, and separate supported explanations from assumptions.

skills.title: Allocate shared costs
skills.description: Draft custom cost axes, preview leftovers and rule overlap, then publish approved allocation rules.

skills.title: Start with the right workflow
skills.description: Choose the Costory tools and detailed skills for spend queries, investigations, budgets, dashboards, reports and alerts.

projects.setup: Requires a Costory workspace with billing data connected and its hosted MCP at https://app-api.costory.io/mcp, authenticated through browser OAuth. Queries use workspace cost data. Preview changes and confirm before publishing allocations, delivering reports or applying schema changes. Each linked skill page includes setup and source details.

projects.name: Extra Caffeine
projects.kind: Local Mac MCP · One workflow skill
projects.headline: Keep your Mac awake while the work needs it.
projects.summary: Give local AI and file-processing work time to finish. The Extra Caffeine workflow guides an agent through authorized awake sessions, state checks and requested one-time schedules while preserving existing sessions.
projects.setup: Requires macOS 14+ and the separately purchased, paid Extra Caffeine 1.2+ app, kept open with AI assistants enabled by the user. Follow the publisher’s setup and license terms. The skill does not install the app or enable access. It prevents idle sleep, not closed-lid sleep, and does not wake a sleeping Mac. No security scan or runtime execution was performed: not scanned; runtime-unverified. Editorial feature only; scored catalog listing is pending the next directory refresh.

capabilities.title: One workflow: extra-caffeine-workflow
capabilities.description: Choose the duration and display behavior, verify awake state, and reconcile timeouts before retrying.

projects.name: Opsibyte
projects.kind: Six skills · Publishing, budgets, listings, and music
projects.headline: Prepare a post, a launch, a workbook, or a practice session.
projects.summary: Six focused workflows combine human-reviewed publishing and launch preparation with local budget, listing-copy, and chord helpers. Each listing carries its own source-derived quality report and setup details.

skills.title: Prepare a social schedule
skills.description: Draft distinct social posts, review account timing, and approve the exact content and schedule before publication.

skills.title: Review blog drafts
skills.description: Connect a publishing destination, explore article topics, and prepare blog drafts for human review.

skills.title: Prepare a product launch
skills.description: Research a product category, prepare an approved Toolfound submission, and track owner verification and launch status.

skills.title: Create a budget workbook

skills.title: Review listing copy

Hosted services were not exercised in this review. Python 3 runs the local helpers. At the reviewed revision, use a new budget filename and calculate net cash flow separately; preserve existing campaign attribution manually. Upstream PR #1 supplies the tested corrections. Each skill page links its exact setup and source.

projects.name: Cisco AI Defense Skill Scanner
projects.headline: Review a skill’s source before you install it.
projects.summary: Inspect skill instructions and bundled code for known prompt-injection, exfiltration and command-execution patterns. The reviewed 2.3.1 release supports local static and behavioral analysis, with machine-readable findings to guide review.

capabilities.title: Inspect source without running the skill
capabilities.description: Combine pattern detection with Python and Bash dataflow analysis. Review the source as data before installing its scripts or hooks.

capabilities.title: Keep evidence with the findings
capabilities.description: Export JSON or SARIF, retain the exact source revision and scanner version, and inspect errors and coverage gaps alongside findings.

capabilities.title: Choose what leaves the machine
capabilities.description: Local analysis can run in an isolated environment with network access disabled. Optional hosted LLM, AI Defense, OSV and VirusTotal routes can send data when enabled.

projects.setup: Use the reviewed 2.3.1 release with verified dependency pins. Exclude the hijacked litellm 1.107.0 release and correct the certifi version in Cisco’s attached release lock. For local source review, disable hosted analyzers and behavioral alignment verification, use a network-disabled container, and retain every finding and error. Automated detection is best effort and does not certify a skill. This is an independent editorial selection, not a Cisco partnership.

projects.name: Geekflare
projects.headline: Turn public web pages into useful data and website checks.
projects.summary: The Geekflare skill guides agents through web search, structured page extraction, metadata, brand assets, screenshots, PDFs and website diagnostics. The reviewed scope is the single geekflare skill at skills/geekflare.
projects.setup: Requires a Geekflare account and GEEKFLARE_API_KEY. Requests send queries, URLs and options to Geekflare and consume account credits; the source documents a free tier. Use public pages and authorized diagnostic targets. Hosted MCP places the key in the URL path, so keep connection URLs out of logs and shared text. The optional local MCP command runs the unpinned npm package @geekflare/mcp. The hosted scraping service advertises CAPTCHA solving and anti-bot handling. REST docs default stealth, proxyMode and renderJS to false; proxyCountry independently enables proxy routing. CAPTCHA fallback behavior is unspecified. The npm runtime and hosted service were not tested.

skills.title: geekflare
skills.description: Choose tools for live search, page data, visual captures and website health checks through Geekflare MCP or its REST API.

projects.name: agent-qa CLI by Vostride
projects.kind: QA agent CLI · Dashboard, MCP and four skills

Licensed under FSL-1.1-ALv2, the Functional Source License: any use other than a competing commercial product or service, with Apache-2.0 terms for each release two years after it is made available.

The app runs locally with your own keys, and requests go to the model and voice providers you configure. Windows and Intel Macs run Frametell from source with Node.js 22.19+ and pnpm. AGPL-3.0 covers the app in this repository.

MIT applies to the two skill folders, prompts/skills/inkroom-prompts and skills/inkroom-prompt-reverse; the repository has no root license. projects.name: Berlin Job Search
projects.kind: One skill · Claude Code and Codex plugin
projects.headline: Job search coaching built for Germany.
projects.summary: An AI job-search coach that knows how hiring works in Germany, Berlin first and Germany-wide. Search live German job sources, check German-language and Blue Card requirements, prepare a Lebenslauf or CV, practise interviews and track applications.

capabilities.title: Find roles
capabilities.description: Search with German and English titles across sources chosen for your field, drop off-target titles and save a ranked shortlist.

capabilities.title: Check a posting
capabilities.description: See the German requirement with the quoted line, the salary against 2026 Blue Card thresholds, and agency and contract terms.

capabilities.title: Apply and interview
capabilities.description: Prepare a German Lebenslauf and Anschreiben or an English CV and letter, checked against your CV, then practise mock interviews with scored feedback.

capabilities.title: Track applications
capabilities.description: Log application news, draft follow-ups and see response rates on an offline dashboard.

projects.setup: Install it as a Claude Code or Codex plugin, or add it to any agent from the repository, then say “Set up my job search.” The bundled scripts need Python 3.9+ (standard library only) and internet access, with no API keys. Your CV, profile and tracker stay on your machine in job-search/. Sources include Bundesagentur für Arbeit, Arbeitnow, Daily Berlin Jobs, company job boards and LinkedIn’s logged-out guest search, which is subject to LinkedIn’s User Agreement. The skill never applies, sends messages or creates accounts for you.

projects.name: lfr
projects.headline: Your own mail server, run by your agent.
projects.summary: One Go binary runs mail for your domains on one small server: mailboxes, and newsletters with their websites. Your agent operates it through the lfr CLI, on the server or over ssh.

capabilities.title: Set up a mail server
capabilities.description: Run lfr setup with your mail hostname, add a domain and publish exactly the DNS records lfr prints; lfr doctor checks them.

capabilities.title: Run mailboxes
capabilities.description: Create addresses, aliases and forwarding, search and answer mail, and train the spam filter as you move messages.

capabilities.title: Publish newsletters
capabilities.description: Run lists with double opt-in and stored consent proof, Markdown issues checked before sending, one-click unsubscribe and a website for each list.

projects.setup: Requires a Linux or macOS server you control and a domain whose DNS you manage. The skill installs lfr with curl -fsSL https://lfr.email/install.sh | sudo sh, which checks the release against its checksums; Homebrew and go install also work. lfr setup creates a hardened systemd service on ports 25, 80 and 443. Where a provider blocks outbound port 25, lfr hands DKIM-signed mail to an SMTP relay such as Amazon SES or SMTP2GO. Your agent asks for explicit approval before sending any message in your name.
